definitions.explanation: Tiny grains of iron-bearing mineral (mostly magnetite) found mixed with ordinary sand on beaches and riverbeds. Magnetic, and historically used in Japan as a raw material for tatara iron-making.

examples.japanese: ⟦{磁石|じしゃく}→磁石：04211_jishaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{砂鉄|さてつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧。
examples.english: Collect iron sand with a magnet.

examples.japanese: ⟦{海岸|かいがん}→海岸：00852_kaigan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{砂|すな}→砂：00890_suna⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{砂鉄|さてつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{混|ま}じっている→混じる：02421_majiru⟧。
examples.english: Iron sand is mixed in with the sand on the beach.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{砂鉄|さてつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{原料|げんりょう}→原料：11802_genryou⟧にして⟦{刀|かたな}→刀：02194_katana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}っていた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: In old Japan, swords were made from iron sand as a raw material.

notes:
Composed of {砂|さ} (sand) + ⟦{鉄|てつ}→鉄：02225_tetsu⟧ (iron). Refers to the dark, magnetic granules found in sand. Famous in Japan for its use in the traditional たたら⟦{製鉄|せいてつ}→製鉄：24078_seitetsu⟧ (tatara iron-making) that produced steel for Japanese swords.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {砂鉄|さてつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧: collect iron sand
- ⟦{磁石|じしゃく}→磁石：04211_jishaku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{砂鉄|さてつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく: iron sand sticks to a magnet
- {砂鉄|さてつ}⟦{採取|さいしゅ}→採取：12901_saishu⟧: iron-sand gathering
- {砂鉄|さてつ}{鉱床|こうしょう}: iron-sand deposit

CULTURAL NOTE:
Iron-sand collection is a common Japanese elementary-school science experiment: children draw a magnet through beach or playground sand to see the dark iron grains gather around it.
